items._cn_summary: Pure Reason Revolution的新专辑在编曲结构上展现出明显的现代意识，吉他riff兼具金属力量与grunge的粗粝感，多层人声处理借鉴了Beach Boys式的精致和声逻辑，同时注入Pink Floyd式的氛围延展。合成器纹理层次丰富，制作人Bruce Soord在混音中保留了足够的呼吸空间，使12分钟同名曲与15分钟尾曲在动静之间形成对比。乐队在传统前卫摇滚框架内尝试了一些电影化的声响探索，歌词的情绪表达与器乐编排紧密咬合。整体而言，这是一张制作精良、细节饱满的前卫摇滚专辑，但在类型创新性上仍偏向守成，未完全突破该流派的既有范式。

items.body: Review by Prog Dog — This is actually a divisive album among devoted Yes fans, mainly because of the absence of key founding member and vocalist Jon Anderson. Gone was his distinct and immediately recognizable high tenor voice, along with the more fanciful and fantasy-like lyrics that had become part of the Yes sound. For others, it may be the departure of keyboardist Rick Wakeman that makes Drama difficult to embrace. Filling his shoes was Geoff Downes, whose keyboard approach was quite different from Wakeman's. Although Downes had considerable classical training, his work on Drama placed greater emphasis on texture, tone and the emerging possibilities of synthesizers and electronic technology, bringing some of the new-wave sensibilities of the Buggles into Yes.I recall that sometime around 1980, or perhaps early 1981, my brother and I had each picked up another Yes album. I got Tormato; he got Drama. Neither of us, as very new Yes fans at the time, realized that Jon Anderson wasn't on Drama. Instead, Trevor Horn, known for his work with the Buggles, had stepped into Anderson's shoes.My brother asked if I wanted to trade. I don't remember whether I agreed or not'I liked both albums equally. If I had based the trade strictly on the album artwork, though, Drama would have won hands down. It's one of Roger Dean's great Yes covers.One of the great tracks on this important album is the opening epic 'Machine Messiah.' For anyone who had become a fan of Steve Howe's guitar work and direction on Tormato, this must have been something of a shock. As the track begins Howe goes all-in on the heavy, riff-driven guitar sound here, venturing into territory that sounds like an early precursor to prog-metal. Not that he hadn't demonstrated an aggressive side before, with tracks such as 'The Gates of Delirium,' 'Close to the Edge,' 'Heart of the Sunrise,' and 'Perpetual Change.' But this was different'a heavier, more metallic approach that, in retrospect, foreshadowed the emergence of that off-shoot of prog-rock.The track changes its palette several times, at one point featuring tentative acoustic guitar and an epic, almost devotional or cultish atmosphere as technology is worshipped and revered. It feels surprisingly prescient today. Another major section is full of hope, though, as Horn reaches for notes his vocal cords could barely have been expected to reach: 'Maybe we'll change / Offered the chance / To finally unlearn our lessons and alter our stance.' 'Man in a White Car' is a little ditty that I wish they had developed into a full-grown song. Instead, it serves nicely as a palette cleanser after the frighteningly epic 'Machine Messiah,' which sounds like it could easily have drawn lightning bolts down from the sky.'Does It Really Happen' features one of Chris Squire's all-time hookiest bass lines. Alan White's sheer power and focus as a drummer is especially potent throughout this album, on this track as on any on Drama. The drums and bass feed off each other with near-ferocity, while the vocals are equally aggressive. Squire's distinctive voice shines through on this one, while Horn's singing is also well showcased. Together, they form something of a power duo.The new-wave vibes are prominent in the opening melodic instrumental section, but there are hints of Yes' Going for the One too, thanks to Steve Howe's distorted pedal steel, with his steel bar swooping between the chords.'Into the Lens' is the oft-overshadowed track on this album, despite showcasing the band's hyper-creativity. Horn provides some more emotional and introspective vocals, with lyrics that seem to explore detachment and observation. Once again, Downes' synths transport Yes firmly into new-wave territory, while the song still holds onto its proggy identity through its numerous passages and sections. There's even a wonderfully eclectic mix of sounds, including sitar and vocoder. Howe also leans into his 'talking guitar' sound, using a wah-wah pedal to make the instrument seem to speak.'Run Through the Light' is a rare and daring track for Yes, featuring Trevor Horn on fretless bass while Squire instead plays some affected piano chords around the track. Horn's vocals add a completely new sound for Yes, with a staccato, almost stuttering effect. It seems likely Squire was coaching Horn through the track, and there's a story that by having Horn play bass, the song was more likely to make the final album cut'something Squire seemed quite determined to ensure.'Tempus Fugit' is a muscular song. Chris Squire provides the fast, heavy bass riffs that hold the whole thing together like the bones of a roller coaster. There's also some early use of the Fairlight CMI in the 'yes, yes, yes, yes' synthetic vocal samples at the end. It's an amusing little break in the fourth wall, with Yes seemingly making a self-conscious reference to itself. I can attest to how effective it was: my first conscious exposure to Yes was hearing this song on the radio, and that repeated 'yes, yes, yes, yes' stuck in my head. After running downstairs to tell my brother about this new band I had discovered, I would soon be buying my first Yes records. Ironically, Drama was one of the last Yes albums my brother and I actually bought in around 1980. This is not Yes's best record, but it is essential nonetheless, chock full of exciting music, and everyone in the band sounds fresh and revitalized. I give it a 4.75 out of 5 dog bones. (5 for prog archives round-ed off score)
items._genre: symphonic prog / progressive rock / new wave
items._cn_summary: 这张1980年的专辑标志着Yes乐队在核心成员变动后的转折。失去了Jon Anderson的高音嗓音和Rick Wakeman的键盘风格，Trevor Horn与Geoff Downes的加入带来了新浪潮的敏感度，键盘音色更注重合成器质地与电子质感。开篇长曲以沉重的金属化吉他riff开场，呈现出前卫金属的早期雏形，随后在声学段落中转入近乎宗教崇拜的氛围，形成多层次色彩变化。Chris Squire标志性的贝斯线条充满hook，Alan White的鼓击力量充沛。专辑融合了重金属元素、新浪潮合成器美学与前卫摇滚的史诗结构，是一支老牌前卫摇滚乐队在新时期探索声音边界的过渡性作品。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 'Tellurian' is the second studio album from Swedish progressive metal band Soen, a relatively newact that features ex-Opeth drummer Martin Lopez alongside vocalist Joel Ekel�f and guitarist JoakimPlatbarzdis, whose sound strongly resembles fellow progressive acts Tool and Leprous, and to alesser extent the alternative metal played by System of a Down and Katatonia. Similarly to theirdebut album 'Cognitive', but with a greater sense of identity, this 2014 release offers a crisp andcontemporary atmospheric progressive metal sound that features a fine balance between technicallyacute guitar riffs and soothing instrumental liquidity that projects itself in the form ofsyncopated rhythms and dense grooves. There is a bit of experimentation going on as well,particularly in the rhythm section, as drummer Martin Lopez lays down some diverse and delightfulgrooves, perhaps channeling his inner Danny Carey. The vocals represent another interesting part ofthis record, as the delivery of Joel Ekel�f is warm and emotive, definitely befitting the etherealstyle of rock that prevails on 'Tellurian'. There is a certain aspect of the album that is touchingand melancholic, while the record itself is consistent and well-structured, with strong entries like'Tabula Rasa', 'Pluton' and 'Void' beautifully depicting Soen's stylistic leanings. At the sametime, some tracks feel drawn out and monotonous, with a lightweight, atmospheric tone that ismaintained for the entire duration of the songs, as heard on 'The Words' or 'The Other's Fall'. Thiscompletely takes away their compositional edge, and it also diminishes the appeal of the strongertracks. Therefore, 'Tellurian' is hardly a groundbreaking prog metal masterpiece; it is more of adriven and consistent collection of songs, which salvages the weaker moments, and presents Soen as agroup searching for a recognizable sound.
items._cn_summary: Soen乐队由前Opeth鼓手Martin Lopez领衔，这张专辑延续了首作的氛围化前卫金属路线，以技术性吉他切分节奏与流畅器乐律动构筑层次。鼓手贡献了多样化的律动设计，颇为出彩；人声温暖而情感化，与专辑的飘渺气质契合。部分曲目如《Tabula Rasa》《Pluton》《Void》展现了乐队的风格倾向，但也有不少曲目因过度依赖轻量化的氛围铺陈而显得冗长单调，削弱了整体的作曲锐度。整体而言，这是一张驱动力与一致性兼备的作品，乐评明确指出它并非突破性的前卫金属杰作，更像是乐队在寻求标志性声音过程中的一次阶段性输出。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — One could understand and appreciate this Muse album only by knowing that the band had attempted tocreate something completely out of the ordinary even by their own standards. An album that has Queenand Skrillex as major influences is meant to be compositionally intense and stylistically chaotic,which is precisely what 'The 2nd Law' is - a collection of epic, theatrical, and electronic-riddenpop rock anthems that broadly explore the concepts of authoritarianism, power-control dynamics aswell as conspiracy and fiction. A fascinating mixture of disparate styles is at stake here, as theband offers an entertaining collection informed by past releases like 'The Resistance', but leaningmore into the artsy electronic side of their music. However, with its thirteen tracks, 'The 2nd Law'is hardly the most consistent release from the British trio. The futuristic production stylehighlights the strong melodies on tracks like 'Animals' and 'Save Me', but it also renders some ofthe mellower songs utterly dull.The stark contrasts between the funky dance pop elements, the hammering rock riffs, the energeticdubstep beats, and the operatic vocal experiments, however, make 'The 2nd Law' somewhat of aschizophrenic listen. This is effective and engaging for a while, especially when the listener ispresented with excellent songs like the Bond movie theme opener 'Supremacy', the electro-poppysingle 'Madness', or the funk rock number 'Panic Station' in the very beginning of the record, butthe effect soon washes away as certain songs begin to resemble Radiohead or Queen way too blatantly.The two Chris Wolstenholme features are quite good, nevertheless, with 'Liquid State' being animportant album highlight, in my opinion, depicting the band's bass player as a strong vocalists andsongwriter. The two closing pieces are quite interesting as well, despite being mostly instrumentaland vastly dubstep-inspired. I still think the use of electronics and digital instruments on thisalbum is one of its stronger features, but the overall mixture of genres and dynamics can easilybecome overwhelming. I would not call 'The 2nd Law' a classic but I definitely feel it is the kindof record only Muse could attempt to produce.
items._cn_summary: 专辑将Queen式的戏剧化摇滚与Skrillex式的电子制作相融合，呈现出风格杂糅的实验倾向。评论指出作品涵盖funky流行、强劲摇滚riff、dubstep节拍与歌剧化人声实验等多重元素，主题涉及独裁与权力控制。前半部分以Bond主题曲开场，辅以电子流行单曲与funk rock曲目，亮点频出；Chris Wolstenholme主唱的两首作品尤为出色，结尾的器乐dubstep段落也颇具趣味。然而风格跨度过于剧烈导致整体听感趋于分裂，后半段部分曲目模仿Radiohead与Queen痕迹过重，柔和曲目在电子化制作下显得乏味。评论者将其视为Muse独有的尝试，但并非经典之作。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items._cn_summary: 专辑以墨西哥牛仔历史上前往夏威夷牧牛的文化线索为概念，将墨西哥传统音乐与夏威夷音乐进行跨文化融合，涵盖西班牙语、夏威夷语和英语三种语言的曲目。制作上以尤克里里、吉他、墨西哥竖琴和手风琴等乐器编织密集编排，邀请Taj Mahal、David Hidalgo等资深乐人参与，由Sonny Lim等夏威夷本土音乐人贡献滑音吉他和夏威夷滑音吉他演奏。录制采用一室同期录音方式，大量即兴段落赋予作品现场感，编曲在传统框架中融入社会评论。整体呈现出墨西哥与夏威夷传统音乐的深层对话，是一次有文化深度的世界音乐跨界合作，但未涉及电子或实验元素，风格偏向传统融合而非前沿实验。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张芬兰手风琴与钢琴二重奏专辑，两位音乐家合作长达三十五年，形成了高度的默契与即兴能力。Kalaniemi以旋律性见长，演奏温柔而优美，Alakotila作为钢琴伴奏者不仅支撑旋律，更加入自己的演绎，使每首作品都成为打磨精致的宝石。专辑以二人演奏为主，Kalaniemi的无词人声在开场传统曲中登场，弦乐四重奏在标题曲中适度扩展层次。曲目涵盖多首原创与传统作品，包括一首Piazzolla的探戈曲及芬兰特色的探戈原创。整体气质安静流畅，如同长长吐息般自然，没有炫技空间，两位乐者专注于旋律本身的探索与享受。评论者认为这张专辑不会震动大地，但提供了真正悦耳的聆听美感。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / sound art
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头录制的枪支暴力幸存者口述合集。录制地点选在一位94岁祖母家的前廊，靠近中途机场降落航线之下，参与者年龄从17岁到67岁不等，多为当地居民。编辑直言这'不是音乐'，但选择以原始环境声与证词并置的方式呈现，试图让被遗忘的社区发声。录音中包含自由式说唱片段，但主体是普通人对暴力创伤的直接讲述，其中一位失去两个儿子的老人反复道歉。录制当天恰逢特朗普下令国民警卫队进驻芝加哥。项目收益将捐给Cure Violence Global。整张作品以社会纪实为内核，声音未经任何后期添加，保留了街道的真实环境音。

items._cn_summary: 本篇内容来自Avant Music News，转发了Fringes of Sound的两则短评，涉及The Last Five Minutes的《Blind End Now》与Stylianos OU的《Moodtoxicosis》。前者由Alberto Carozzi与Matteo Uggeri合作，以贝斯、笔记本电脑处理、黑胶循环和松散结构的打击乐构建声响，介于即兴与拼贴之间。后者以碎片化人声、不规则打击乐和噪音摇滚段落为核心，呈现一段关于癌症主题的实验叙事。文本为转载性质，并非完整原创乐评，信息有限，但所涉艺术家的手法契合实验/前卫音乐场景，融合即兴、电子处理与噪音美学，具有一定先锋色彩。

items._cn_summary: 巴尔的摩吉他手将个人挣扎转化为冷峻、不安的俱乐部声响。文章描述SUAHN的这张作品以post-hardcore为底色，融入实验元素和俱乐部舞曲结构，试图在硬核的冲击感与电子节奏之间建立联系。文中提及"俱乐部即兴"式的编排暗示其偏向节奏化与机械感的方向，而非传统后硬核的吉他主导叙事。由于原文仅为简短摘要，缺乏对具体编曲手法、声音设计或音乐结构的深入描述，无法判断其在实验层面的实际深度。整体而言，该作品在风格上与暗潮、工业电子等领域有一定距离感的交叉，但核心仍植根于后硬科这一更偏摇滚谱系的类型。

Sometimes we do this speculatively, through other people’s lives. This kind of speculation also drives the discourse around Joy Division’s brief and tragic history. A reason to look anew at this well-thumbed tale is the release of an official collection of live audio and video recordings - with unreleased, often brilliant material. It has a canny name: Eternal (Live). The music and video is accompanied by epoch-defining images from the celebrated band photographers,... items._cn_summary: 本文围绕即将发行的Joy Division官方现场录音合集展开，重新审视这支乐队在现场舞台上的强劲表现，与录音室作品中常被讨论的悲剧叙事形成对照。文章指出，这套名为Eternal (Live)的合集收录了过去鲜少公开的现场音频与视频素材，配以知名乐队摄影师所拍摄的标志性影像。作者借由人们习惯通过他人故事来构建叙事的现象切入，提醒读者：在Joy Division短暂的传奇之外，还有另一重面目——那些在欧洲与英国巡演中以现场实力征服观众的瞬间。整体定位更接近一篇资讯导引而非深度乐评，可供对该乐队现场遗产感兴趣的听众参考，但对声音细节、编曲结构与现场表现力的分析极为有限。

items._cn_summary: 这是对A Certain Ratio两张经典专辑《The Joy of Sextet》（1982）和《Force Majeure》（1986）的重新发行项目。评论指出乐队自2020年以来已发行了三张新专辑，此次档案挖掘虽曾引发创意枯竭的担忧，但实际呈现的是两张风格迥异的周年纪念版本，附带全新混音、调整后的曲目编排以及一些意料之外的惊喜内容。文章属于发行公告性质，对音乐本身的分析极为有限，且内容截断不完整，无法深入了解两张专辑的重新诠释方式及其艺术价值。作为曼彻斯特后朋克场景的代表乐队的档案再版项目，与实验、前卫或电子等深度偏好领域的关联度较弱。

items.body: Review by toroddreincarnated — The second album from this band from Norway.The band was a duo with a line-up of double bass, bass, guitars, keyboards, concertina, effects andvocals.A number of guests added drums, violins, strings and trumpet.This is the follow-up album to their 2024 debut album Bridge Of Sighs from 2024. An album I reviewedback in April 2024 in # 3 of my blog The Sound Of Fighting Cats. I gave it a three stars review.Lullabies for the Marooned clocks in at three quarters of an hour.The music here is art-rock.The band, I mean duo, has retreated from the more rocking soundscape on their debut album into amuch more intimate, softly spoken and refined soundscape on their new album, the follow-up album.Early Genesis, Procol Harum, Sylvan, Talk Talk and Peter Hammill are good references here. There areeven some Steve Hogarth era Marillion lurking around in their music too. There is a blend of acoustic and electric instruments here, including guitars. The strings is addinga lot of colours and are complementing the great vocals.This is an album where a piece of music crosses over to becoming an artwork. The result is a great album and one of this year's better albums from Norway, the new powerhouse inart-rock and prog rock. 4 stars
items._genre: art rock / crossover prog / chamber pop
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自挪威的双人组合的第二张专辑，编制涵盖低音提琴、贝斯、吉他、键盘、手风琴及人声，并邀请客座乐手加入鼓、小提琴、弦乐和 trumpet。与首张专辑相比，他们从较为摇滚化的声音转向了更内敛、柔和、精致的气质。Early Genesis、Procol Harum、Sylvan、Talk Talk、Peter Hammill 以及 Steve Hogarth 时期的 Marillion 是主要的风格参照。弦乐与人声在这里形成细腻的色彩对比，专辑整体时长约四十五分钟，试图将乐曲提升为艺术作品。从风格定位来看，这属于偏向传统艺术摇滚和前卫摇滚范畴的作品，虽然带有一定的精致感和内省气质，但在实验性、电子元素、即兴维度或跨界融合方面较为有限，与用户关注的实验前卫、学院派爵士、电子、世界音乐、暗潮等方向差距较大。

items.body: Review by alainPP — NORTH SEA ECHOES, nothing new except for extending their first offering: heavier, more melancholic, more pervasive."A Time of Innocence and Purpose," with its bass and hypnotic, unsettling electro sample, is featured on LUNATIC SOUL. A beautiful ascent with Ray taking the lead, where things become much more interesting. A kind of GILDENLOW and pugnacious OSI hybrid, thanks to that captivating voice that makes all the difference. The ambient, intimate atmosphere makes you close your eyes and dream along to the edgy riff. "Enjoy The View" delves deeper into the electro-synthetic sound with its two-tone vocals and addictive instrumentation. The industrial riff, a sound effect on the thunderous breakdown, the keyboard undulating in a new dark-wave style. The magic works and endures with the energy of the invigorating chorus over the haunting verse, the haunting, dark outro. "Good Enough" features a crystalline, airy, stereo acoustic arpeggio reminiscent of the good old days. The raw, spoken-word vocals are laid over it, creating a country evening feel. The warm crescendo, with Ray as the sonic hero, evokes a dark Louisiana vibe with animals singing in the background: sublime and utterly simple, surfing on the atmospheric. "I'll Leave A Light On" kicks off with a fat riff, a melancholic nod to Katatonia. The pre-screamed vocals over the powerful sound, the chorus like something out of the mainstream era: the nostalgia is amplified by a punchy guitar solo bursting with notes. An added choir graces this track, which flows effortlessly, nothing new but well executed, finally on Fates Warning. "All Fall Away" boasts a bouncy bass beat. A dark, monolithic feel, redolent of Eurythmics in a heavy version, for this primal alternative drift. The guitar twists and turns, illuminating the space, the beat becomes oppressive, reminiscent of PARADISE LOST with Ray's voice, the chorus, then the beat abruptly stopping."Revenge," with its Wavy-esque guitar, surfs on the scales of THE CURE. This decadent rock descends to the realm of electro-pop, a softer DEPECHE MODE, Ray bribing his vocal cords. A repetitive, melancholic finale, far removed from prog rock. "Villains Or Saints" returns to mainstream, mainstream rock with its heavy melody, surfing once again on FATES WARNING. The haunting, synthetic rhythm builds and creates a heavy guitar space over the velvety keyboard. Ray conducts this masterful string piece, always effortless yet captivating, this timeless ballad. "What Is And What Was What," with its dark, ambient, mysterious intro and that wind that seems to come from nowhere. Vocals over a guitar arpeggio, choir over organ, hairs shiver. The bass resonates, clears the speakers, the pleasure of having this vibrant, body-piercing sound, like an arrow piercing your heart. "All That Comes After" returns to edgy rock, energized by its catchy melody. A B-side track that doesn't offer anything new, however, except perhaps to test the stereo image on the atmospheric drift. This melodic sound takes you back to the previous millennium. "How To Cast A Shadow" concludes, the new-wave vibe with its heady keyboard, as fat as the 'metroganic' drums, Ray weaving through this dark, hybrid, alternative slow jam. The mantra-like latency for dancing, swaying with his wife, the guitar both melancholic and slide-like. The feeling of navigating a bayou. A heavy guitar solo, the sound that makes you headbang, the refrain of 80s hard rock bands, I'm sucked into this musical spiral. The finale features Ray clinging to the primal synth, shh... Silence remains a constant presence throughout the album, with its enveloping notes.NORTH SEA ECHOES pushes their identity further with a heavy, dark approach, evolving with the addition of electronic elements to delve into the ghosts of the past, temptation, and reflection. (3.75)
items._cn_summary: 北回声乐队延续前作路线，整体偏向沉重与忧郁的气质。评论将作品与多个乐队进行类比，涵盖工业合成器音色、新浪潮式的双色调人声处理，以及Katatonia式的忧郁金属质感。专辑在器乐编排上呈现出电子合成与吉他音墙的交替运用，人声时而低语时而呐喊，层次较为丰富。然而，从评论描述来看，这张专辑并未在实验性或前卫性上做出显著突破，更多是在已有风格框架内进行扩展与混合，歌曲结构以旋律性为主，缺乏真正意义上的前卫探索。对于偏好实验、前卫与即兴的听众而言，这张作品的创新性与独特性较为有限，更接近于带有暗色调的另类摇滚与主流摇滚的融合产物。

items.body: Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart reissue the 2xCD collection “The Usual Suspects” on Dimple Discs on November 13, 2026. Originally released in 2017, the 23-track set has been unavailable for years and now changes hands at collectors’ prices; the digital edition is already available on Bandcamp, with the physical 2xCD prepared for that November date to coincide with a UK and Belgium tour. Usual Suspects by Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart “The Usual Suspects” gathers new recordings of Wobble’s solo material alongside songs from Invaders Of The Heart and his former band Public Image Ltd (PiL), drawn from a catalogue spanning almost forty years at the time of recording. The album was recorded at The Smokehouse studios in East London and opens with a version of PiL’s debut single “Public Image”, reworked from the band’s 1978 debut album. Other highlights include cover versions of the film themes to “Midnight Cowboy” and “Get Carter”, Dawn Penn’s “You Don’t Love Me (No, No, No)” featuring vocalist Aurora Dawn, and a new take on “Visions Of You”, which originally featured Sinéad O’Connor on Invaders Of The Heart’s Mercury Prize-nominated 1992 album “Rising Above Bedlam”. The set closes with live recordings of “Liquidator” and “Poptones”, the latter drawn from PiL’s “Metal Box”. Recording personnel on “The Usual Suspects” comprised Jah Wobble on bass, vocals and percussion, Marc Layton-Bennett on drums, percussion and backing vocals, Martin Chung on guitars, George King on keyboards and backing vocals, Steve Rigby on programming and backing vocals, Sean Corby on trumpet and flugelhorn, Aurora Dawn on vocals, and Holly Macve on vocals. Of the band behind the album, Wobble said: “This band has been a delight to play with. Similar to my first early ’80s version of the Invaders, they can all really play, plus all genre bases […] are covered. It’s a big deal to me, because it’s like a 35 year old dream has finally been realised. This is how I heard The Invaders of the Heart sound all those years ago. A classy fusion of genres. Groovy, dubby but always changing and developing. Never standing still.” Tour dates for Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart The reissue follows a UK tour and comes ahead of Belgian dates in November. Confirmed shows: October 3 – Stourbridge, Katie Fitzgerald’s (UK) October 16 – Todmorden, Unitarian Church (UK) October 21 – Frome, The Tunnels (UK) October 22 – Bristol, The Fleece (UK) October 23 – Reading, Face Bar (UK) November 7 – London, Bush Hall (UK) November 25 – Hasselt, Club AFF (Belgium) November 26 – Bruges, Cactus Muziekcentrum (Belgium) November 27 – Oudenaarde, Harmonie Oudenaarde (Belgium) Tickets are available via Songkick. About Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart Jah Wobble, born John Wardle, is a bass guitarist and vocalist from East London who was the original bassist in Public Image Ltd alongside John Lydon from the band’s 1978 formation, co-writing and playing on the 1979 album “Metal Box” before leaving in late 1980. He formed Jah Wobble’s Invaders Of The Heart in 1982, and in the early 1980s collaborated with Holger Czukay and Jaki Liebezeit of Can, as well as U2 guitarist The Edge and producer François Kevorkian. Invaders Of The Heart’s commercial peak came with 1991’s “Rising Above Bedlam”, nominated for the Mercury Prize, which included the UK top-40 single “Visions Of You” featuring Sinéad O’Connor. Wobble has since worked with artists including Ginger Baker, Björk, Brian Eno, Baaba Maal, Massive Attack, Sinéad O’Connor, Pharoah Sanders and his wife Zi Lan Liao on guzheng and harp. He reunited with former PiL guitarist Keith Levene in 2012 for the “Metal Box in Dub” shows and the album “Yin & Yang”. Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart recorded “The Usual Suspects” at The Smokehouse studios in East London, releasing it in 2017 following a six-month UK tour, as covered by Side-Line at the time. More recently, Wobble released the albums “Dub, Vol 1” (2025) and “Automated Paradise” (2026, with former Siouxsie & The Banshees guitarist Jon Klein) on Dimple Discs, and “Mystic Liverpool: The Beatles Psychedelic Songbook” with his sons, who record as Tian Qiyi, released by Cherry Red in August 2026. His autobiography, “Memoirs of a Geezer: Music, Life, Mayhem”, was published by Serpent’s Tail in 2009 and reissued in expanded form as “Dark Luminosity” by Faber & Faber in 2024. Dimple Discs now reissues “The Usual Suspects” as a 2xCD on November 13, 2026, timed to Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart’s UK and Belgium tour dates.
items._cn_summary: Jah Wobble 与 The Invaders Of The Heart 重新发行2017年双CD合辑，收录了对PiL时期作品的重新演绎，包括1978年首张单曲《Public Image》、电影配乐《Midnight Cowboy》与《Get Carter》的翻唱，以及与Aurora Dawn合作的Dawn Penn经典曲目。录制于东伦敦Smokehouse录音室，乐队编制涵盖贝斯、鼓、吉他、键盘、铜管及人声，呈现出dub律动与多种风格的融合。专辑以PiL《Metal Box》中的《Poptones》现场录音作结。原文为新闻通稿性质，缺乏深度乐评内容，仅介绍发行信息、曲目列表、乐队成员及巡演日程，未对音乐本身进行艺术性分析。Wobble本人提及这是一次融合多种风格的尝试，但实际风格偏向有根基的dub与post-punk传统，与极端实验或前卫路线有距离。

items.body: Nine Inch Nails released their third studio album, “The Fragile,” through Nothing Records and Interscope Records on 21 September 1999. The industrial rock record arrived as a double album of 23 tracks running one hour and 43 minutes, split across two discs titled “Left” and “Right.” It turns 27 this year. Five years separated “The Fragile” from “The Downward Spiral.” Trent Reznor recorded and mixed the album at Nothing Studios in New Orleans between 1997 and 1999, producing it with Alan Moulder, who also engineered and mixed. Steve Albini handled supplemental drum recording at his Electrical Audio in Chicago, Tom Baker mastered at Precision Mastering, and Bob Ezrin was credited for final continuity and flow. Dr. Dre assisted with the mix on “Even Deeper.” Danny Lohner played guitars on six tracks and contributed drum programming and synthesizers, Adrian Belew added guitar to “Just Like You Imagined,” “The Great Below” and “Where Is Everybody?”, and Mike Garson played piano on “Just Like You Imagined,” “The Way Out Is Through” and “Ripe (With Decay).” Bill Rieflin drummed on “La Mer” alongside vocalist Denise Milfort, Jerome Dillon supplied chorus drums on “We’re in This Together,” and Charlie Clouser, Keith Hillebrandt and Steve Duda covered programming and sound design. David Carson took art direction, design and photography. Disc one, “Left,” runs “Somewhat Damaged,” “The Day the World Went Away,” “The Frail,” “The Wretched,” “We’re in This Together,” “The Fragile,” “Just Like You Imagined,” “Even Deeper,” “Pilgrimage,” “No, You Don’t,” “La Mer” and “The Great Below.” Disc two, “Right,” runs “The Way Out Is Through,” “Into the Void,” “Where Is Everybody?”, “The Mark Has Been Made,” “Please,” “Starfuckers, Inc.,” “Complication,” “I’m Looking Forward to Joining You, Finally,” “The Big Come Down,” “Underneath It All” and “Ripe (With Decay).” Three singles came from the album: “The Day the World Went Away” on 20 July 1999, “We’re in This Together” on 27 September 1999 and “Into the Void” on 10 January 2000, with “Starfuckers, Inc.” issued as a promotional single. The album entered the Billboard 200 at number one with first-week sales of 229,000 copies, the band’s first chart-topping album, then fell to number 16 the following week. The RIAA certified it double platinum on 4 January 2000, and it had sold 898,000 copies in the United States by May 2005. The US edition appeared as a two-CD tri-fold digipak; the three-LP vinyl pressing carried two tracks absent from the CD, “10 Miles High” and “The New Flesh,” and came in a gatefold sleeve with a 24-page booklet. In 2017 the album was reissued on vinyl as a Definitive Edition alongside “The Fragile: Deviations 1,” a limited four-LP instrumental set that was not pressed to CD. The album streams on Spotify. Sources differ on the exact day: MusicBrainz lists 20 September 1999, while Wikipedia, Discogs and Spotify all give 21 September 1999. About Nine Inch Nails Trent Reznor formed Nine Inch Nails in Cleveland, Ohio in 1988, writing and recording the project’s material during off-hours at Right Track Studio, where he worked as an engineer and janitor. TVT Records issued the debut album, “Pretty Hate Machine,” on 20 October 1989. The “Broken” EP followed in 1992, by which point Reznor had negotiated the Nothing Records imprint through Interscope, and “The Downward Spiral” arrived in 1994. Side-Line covered the 2019 book “Into The Never”, which examined that album’s cultural reach, and reported that Johnny Cash initially resisted recording “Hurt”, the “Downward Spiral” track he covered in 2002. “The Fragile” closed the 1990s for the band, and the remix album “Things Falling Apart” followed in 2000. Reznor returned with “With Teeth” in 2005, “Year Zero” in 2007, and both “Ghosts I-IV” and “The Slip” in 2008. Atticus Ross became a full member ahead of “Hesitation Marks” in 2013, and the pair have scored film and television alongside the band since. Side-Line has since reported on Reznor’s appearance on the deluxe vinyl reissue of the 1990 Pigface debut, the Future Ruins festival announced by Reznor and Ross in 2025, the “TRON Ares: Divergence” companion album, and the “Nine Inch Noize” collaboration with Boys Noize released in April 2026. “The Fragile” turns 27 this year, the record that took the band to number one in the United States for the first time.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非乐评，而是Nine Inch Nails第三张录音室专辑《The Fragile》发行27周年的纪念性新闻资讯。内容涵盖专辑的制作人员、录音地点、发行厂牌、曲目列表以及商业成绩等基本信息，未对音乐本身进行任何评论性分析。Trent Reznor与Alan Moulder在新奥尔良Nothing Studios完成制作，Steve Albini负责补充鼓录音，Bob Ezrin把控最终连贯性。专辑以双碟形式发行，首周销量22.9万登顶Billboard 200，并获RIAA双白金认证。然而文章缺乏对声音设计、实验性元素或音乐内涵的探讨，纯粹是事实罗列，对实验音乐爱好者参考价值有限。

items.body:
CLOSE YOUR EYES are kicking off their next chapter with 'Open Your Eyes'.

Released on 18 September, the pre-release single serves as the first taste of the seven-member K-pop group's upcoming fourth mini album, 256th Note. It follows their third mini album, blackout, which arrived in November 2025.

'Open Your Eyes' brings together jazz, hip-hop and R&B, pairing an experimental piano arpeggio loop with fast-paced drums. The track also features pianist Yohan Kim and jazz saxophonist Jacob Scesney, whose performances add to its jazz-influenced sound.

The release continues CLOSE YOUR EYES' musical evolution following their debut with first mini album ETERNALT in April 2025. Formed through reality competition PROJECT7, the group comprises JEON MINWOOK, MA JINGXIANG, JANG YEOJUN, KIM SUNGMIN, SONG SEUNGHO, KENSHIN, and SEO KYOUNGBAE.

items.body: From its roots as a music blog to a fiercely independent label built around physical releases, Somewherecold Records has grown from Jason Lamoreaux’s love of experimental music into a deeply personal effort to give artists and their work something lasting to hold onto. There’s (still) a chill in the air… Déka by The Corrupting Sea   When did Somewherecold Records start, and what was your inspiration? Jason Lamoreaux :: The original version of the label was a partnership with another label in Texas. I think we put out 8 or so albums with them. In 2008, the blog shut down for really accidental reasons and I wanted to start it back up again in 2016. Part of the initiative was the fact that I started to record under The Corrupting Sea and wanted to put my own music out because I thought no one else would care (I’m glad I was very wrong). Anyway, I was a shoegaze DJ at the time and ran into The Beremy Jet‘s EPs but they had no physical release. For me, digital only is a travesty for many albums. I’m very much a physical media person because the entire package is the album. I love putting artwork together, getting the right combination of packaging, and offering the world something to actually hold. Perhaps that’s the Gen Xer in me but I can’t get beyond it really. So, once The Beremy Jets was on board, I began reaching out to folks I had interviewed or reviewed or I was a fan of and brought some into the label. As of now, the roster has been whittled down extensively due to money, health issues, and just the world in general seeming to reject art (perhaps out of financial desperation or something other). At the end of the day, I just want to leave something beautiful behind in this world. The structure of the label is very much inspired by Daniel Miller and the early Mute Records approach to artists. He did it right with honor. He can sleep at night while I don’t know how other record label CEOs can (I’m speaking primarily about major labels that rip off their artists). Anyway, That’s the short of it. Who were some of your initial artist relations, and did your location help or hinder progress? Jason Lamoreaux :: I started the label while living in Texas. I hadn’t gotten to the point where I wanted to play live or even had figured out how to do so with what I was putting together. The location however was great because there are so many experimental artists in Dallas and Austin and getting to cut my teeth live in those places was a huge challenge and inspiration. I didn’t get any on the label till later for some reason, but the label was young and others had different outlets. Initial artists included Aidan Baker, Ummagma, Mis+ress, Yellow6, Niev, Zombie Girlfriend, Thee Koukouvaya, Winterwood, and then my projects like The Corrupting Sea, The Warm Jets, and more came later. I think I’ve worked with around 50 artists over the years. What were some challenges of starting the label, and how did you envision it standing apart? Jason Lamoreaux :: I’m not sure how to answer this except the Somewherecold reputation was well received in the music world because we did a lot of work on interviews and reviews between 2000-2008. I initially started the blog up again with interviews from God is an Astronaut and The Album Leaf but the label side of things started to overwhelm and I decided to move in that direction for the time being. The label is curated by me and I guess that’s the thread through the label. Walls of sound, intimate ambience, electronic experimental, cowboy drone, and other genres are, for me, deeply connected and I wanted the label to reflect my love for those things. Further, I’m an artist. I wanted to be an artist available to other artists. It felt like purpose and, in many ways, still does. What is your motivation in keeping the label moving forward into the next decade? Jason Lamoreaux :: This is a constant question in the back of my mind. I would love for it take off and people to actually support it in full. We don’t press very many physical copies but the current landscape makes it almost impossible to sell out it seems. There is a lot of noise out there, too many algorithms, and a ton of cynicism. So, in my mind, I’m taking it year by year. Once it becomes too onerous, I will likely walk away and maybe keep me and a few collective artists to keep it going. But, for now, we stay the course. That said, Elasticstage in the UK has made it possible to release so much music on vinyl and CDs over on the European side of things. My first 10 The Corrupting Sea albums are now up for order there as well as all the new releases for the label. It’s a press on demand site and the products are beautiful and sound great. The shipping is very low if you order 3 items (their limite right now per order) at a time. “There is a lot of noise out there, too many algorithms, and a ton of cynicism. So, in my mind, I’m taking it year by year.” ~Jason Lamoureaux How do you deliver the label’s “sound” to listeners and fans (through distribution, campaigns, live shows, word of mouth, etc.)? Jason Lamoreaux :: There are a number of ways. I have a rather large promo email system but that is also an issue since so many get inundated with requests for review, etc (I know you probably get the same). The label does have distribution through The Business in Anacortes, Washington. The place is run by this amazing couple and I wish folks would use them more. Again, getting above the noise as it were. Most of my artists play live but I don’t see that as a deal breaker. A Journey of Giraffes is a studio project and has been so well received. Others are new and I’m not sure if they will play live or not. Again, not a deal breaker. I think people can enjoy music outside of the live world especially considering how terrible support for local artists has become in those live spaces. In terms of word of mouth, well, the silence can be deafening. As a label owner, you often have no idea what fans are thinking, if the label is being well received, or artists being listened to until you bump into someone who tells you differently. You would think that with the mountain of communication options, you would hear things. But you don’t and it can get quite lonely. I do post on social media but I’m beginning to see it as a hindrance rather than a plus. The label is heavily pro-lgbtq+, anti-war, pro-immigrants, and more. The people who run these sites have proven to be otherwise and it’s becoming more and more difficult to justify any presence on Social Media. At this moment, plans are being sorted to go to a singular website with Bandcamp attached and nothing more. Lastly, I have uploaded to streaming, which, financially, is a joke. Does it capture people’s attention? I have no idea. You have to have so many streams even to make a penny. I’m behind on those uploads but the label is in a moment of organization and I’ll be uploading past albums that I’ve missed due to daily life. For me, streaming is not a priority. For the same reasons I dislike social media, I dislike streaming companies even more. Spotify, for me, is now a no go. I refuse to place my own music up there but my other artists are welcome to on their own. I don’t control their music. The Déka box set is encased in a purple velvet box set. It contains the first 10 albums remastered by Jason T. Lamoreaux. All come in artwork matching the box. Also, each album except for Ontology has a brand new track attached as a hidden track. Visit Somewherecold Records: Bandcamp | Somewherecold.net Déka by The Corrupting Sea The post Five questions with Somewherecold Records first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统意义上的乐评，而是一篇对Somewherecold Records厂牌主理人Jason Lamoreaux的专访式报道。文章追溯了该厂牌从音乐博客转型为专注于实体发行的独立厂牌的历程，涵盖其成立初衷、与艺术家的合作关系以及在数字时代坚持实体介质的理念。受访者表达了对实验音乐的热爱，提到了Aidan Baker、Yellow6等合作艺术家，以及自身The Corrupting Sea项目。尽管涉及暗潮、自赏派、氛围等风格标签，但由于内容以厂牌运营和创始人故事为主，缺乏对具体音乐作品的深入分析与聆听价值评判，对希望了解相关音乐质地和创作手法的读者参考有限。

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — Once again fabulously illustrated by Annette Appleton in a captivating pictorial style?part na�ve, part naturalistic, and slightly dreamlike?*Estanyo Nord* is the last album by the English duo The Light Afternoon, aka Steve Newland, the ultra-perfectionist multi-instrumentalist, and Annette Appleton, the singer-illustrator with a shy, fairy-like voice. To illustrate the cover of *Estanyo Nord* and the inside poster, Annette was determined to depict the Panorama house and its surroundings as a veritable Garden of Eden, with a profusion of very real animals?mostly birds and cats, but also dogs and a gecko?in a visionary and imaginative style that makes this miraculous bestiary seem surreal and symbolic.The album tells the story of this exotic miniature Walden, a little lost paradise, just a stone's throw from the road and a short walk from the sea, and of its inhabitants? whether human (Ana Cirema and all the other souls of the household) or non-human?mostly cats ("Our Time In The Tin North")?who thrived in Panorama under a dark velvet sky streaked with shooting stars. Conceptually and structurally, *Estanyo Nord* is divided into two distinct parts ("Part One: Anacirema," "Part Two: Estanyo Nord"), like the two sides of a vinyl record, each consisting of four tracks, 4 or 5 minutes per track, for a total running time of 38 minutes?thus respecting the spirit and constraints of vinyl records from their heyday. All of this is significant because *Estanyo Nord* draws heavily on the past?from nostalgic memories of Steve and Annette's personal histories to the musical past of everyone who lived through the '80s to the fullest, in a way that was deceptively carefree yet truly full of hope, filled with both certainties and doubts. " "I don't know what makes me happy, I just know what makes me sad, I do my best to remember all the things that make me glad" ("All Of These Things," luminous memories of Malta, France, and Spain) "Musically, Estanyo Nord is very different from our previous album because Steve didn't want to make *The History of Mr. Puffin Man?The Sequel*" (dixit Annette). One couldn't put it better. As dynamic and assertive as the previous album was languid, gentle, and undulating, *Estanyo Nord* has categorically moved away from the dark symphonic prog of La Renaissance or Dead Can Dance, with the instrumental sounds and rhythmic programming here very clearly oriented toward synth-pop. But both albums share the same melancholy and a highly cinematic approach to music, with subtle touches of modulation and tense minor chords. This is particularly evident from the very start of "Wide Open Highway Road Movie," with its *Midnight Express*-like atmosphere, its sharp guitar chords and solos set against highway rhythms, and its synths so distinctly '80s that you can almost hear that faint vintage hiss that followed each synth note, following the strange hum of the electric current that had set them vibrating. With a slower sequenced tempo, "The Girl from Panorama" is more reminiscent of Kraftwerk or the early Human League. Meanwhile, the more high-energy "Anacirema" and "Estanyo Nord"?true hit potential?blend new wave rock and dance music much as New Order did a few years ago. Those who enjoyed the symphonic harmonies of *The History Of Mr Puffin Man* might prefer "The Paradero" and "All of These Things," with their delicate, haunting melodies, piano arpeggios, mysterious or commanding synths, subtle vocal arrangements, and that guitar that reminds me of Pulsar's *Gorlitz* (1989) in a slightly decadent, fin-de-si�cle (20th-century) atmosphere that evokes Bowie's legendary and unconventional *Low*. This European atmosphere is present with even more tenderness and romanticism on the slow "Watching the Perseids," a small, classically influenced pocket symphony. "Our Time in the Tin North" is closer to the atmospheric post-prog of Soup or North Atlantic Oscillation or the dreamy electronica of Tangerine Dream's latest albums, which should appeal to most of us. But regardless of our musical preferences and how open-minded we are in this regard, it would be a shame to miss this precious opportunity to own such an artistic work?one that is as valuable for its visual presentation as for its musical content. At first glance, it may seem relatively far removed from the usual canons of progressive rock, but ultimately, it is as universal as beauty itself.
items._cn_summary: 英国二人组合The Light Afternoon的专辑以概念专辑形式构建，将叙事分为两部分共八首曲目，整体时长38分钟，刻意遵循黑胶唱片的格式约束。音乐风格从前作的暗色交响前卫转向合成器流行，具有明显的80年代复古音色特征，吉他与合成器交织形成公路电影般的画面感。专辑讲述了Panorama居所及其人畜共居的微观世界，视觉部分由歌手Annette Appleton以梦幻插画呈现。然而整体走向偏向复古怀旧的合成器流行和艺术流行，与用户关注的实验、前卫、电子、暗潮等口味有较大距离，创新性主要体现在概念叙事与视觉呈现层面，音乐本身的实验元素有限。

items.body: Clan of Xymox, the Dutch darkwave and gothic rock project led by Ronny Moorings, released “Notes From The Underground” on 21 September 2001 through Pandaimonium Records in Europe. The album turns 25 this year. Metropolis Records issued it in North America nine days later, on 30 September 2001. Moorings wrote, recorded and mixed all twelve tracks, and produced the record with Mojca Zugna. It was the third studio album of the reformed Clan of Xymox era, after “Hidden Faces” from 1997 and “Creatures” from 1999. Three of its songs were already in circulation by the time it appeared. The “Liberty” CD single, issued by Pandaimonium on 20 October 2000 alongside the band’s double live album, carried “Liberty” together with “Number One” and “At Your Mercy”. Clan of Xymox’s ‘Notes From The Underground’ tracklist and credits The CD runs twelve tracks: “Innocent”, “I Want You Now”, “Internal Darkness”, “At Your Mercy”, “Anguish”, “Number One”, “Into Her Web”, “The Bitter Sweet”, “Liberty”, “Something Wrong”, “Mysterium” and “The Same Dream”. Dierk Budde mastered the album and Mojca Zugna made the sleeve artwork. The band’s official biography states the record reached number 2 on the German DAC chart and topped the US Musicfolio poll for 2001. The same page quotes a Side-Line review of the album as reading “This album is to be seen as a milestone in the band’s discography towards which their previous efforts all converge, or emerge from.” Pandaimonium returned to the material in May 2002 with “Remixes From The Underground”, a two-disc set that reworked every song on the album. Its contributors included Front 242, Assemblage 23, In Strict Confidence, Iris, Angels & Agony and Beborn Beton, and the limited edition added the band’s first video disc. Notes from the Underground by Clan Of Xymox About Clan of Xymox Ronny Moorings formed the band in 1981 in Nijmegen, the Netherlands. Its first release, the mini-album “Subsequent Pleasures”, appeared in 1983 in a run of 500 copies recorded on a four-track home setup. Demo material sent with it led to a deal with 4AD, and the self-titled album followed in 1985, cut at Palladium Studios in Edinburgh and co-produced with label head Ivo Watts-Russell. “Medusa” came next on the same label, and the band contributed “Muscoviet Musquito” to the 4AD compilation “Lonely Is An Eyesore” in 1987. The group parted with 4AD in October 1988, signed to Wing, a PolyGram subsidiary, and shortened its name to Xymox. “Twist of Shadows” arrived in 1989 with the singles “Obsession”, “Imagination” and “Blind Hearts”; the band’s official biography puts its sales above 300,000 copies. “Phoenix” followed in 1991 and closed the Wing chapter when PolyGram wound the label down. “Metamorphosis” and “Headclouds” then came out on the UK independent Zok Records. Moorings also wrote music for two CD-ROM games in the same period, “Total Mayhem” in 1996 and “Revenant” a year later. In 1997 Moorings ended the Xymox era, restarted the band as Clan of Xymox and signed to Tess Records. “Hidden Faces” appeared that year, produced by Dave M. Allen and John A. Rivers. “Creatures” followed in 1999, mixed by Rivers and Moorings, and moved the band to Metropolis Records in North America and Pandaimonium Records in Europe, the pairing that would also handle “Notes From The Underground”. The double live album “LIVE”, drawn from the band’s South and Central American shows, came out in October 2000. “Farewell” arrived in 2003, and “The Best Of Clan Of Xymox”, with its running order chosen by a fan poll, in September 2004. The “Weak In My Knees” EP opened 2006 ahead of the album “Breaking Point”. In early 2009 the band moved to Trisol Records in Europe while staying with Metropolis in the United States, and “In Love We Trust” came out on 18 August 2009, covered in Clan of Xymox’s ‘In Love We Trust’ turns 17 on 18 August. The thirteenth studio album “Darkest Hour” followed on 20 May 2011, the covers set “Kindred Spirits” in October 2012 and “Matters Of Mind, Body And Soul” on 14 February 2014. “Days Of Black” arrived on 7 April 2017, reported in Clan Of Xymox return with new album: ‘Days Of Black’. “Spider On The Wall” followed in 2020, announced in New Clan Of Xymox album ‘Spider On The Wall’ and video for ‘All I Ever Know’, and Moorings talked through his writing that September in Interview with Clan Of Xymox: ‘For Me A Lot Of These Memories Are Finished Stories Without A Soundtrack’. “Limbo”, written during the pandemic lockdowns, arrived in July 2021 and was previewed in Clan Of Xymox returns with all new album ‘Limbo’ in July. The eighteenth album “Exodus” followed in June 2024, reported in Clan Of Xymox announce new album for June: ‘Exodus’, with the “Blood of Christ” EP later that year and a 3CD edition of “Exodus” in February 2025. Moorings looked back across the full run in Ronny Moorings (Clan Of Xymox), an exclusive retrospective interview. Moorings has been the only constant member and still writes, records and produces the band’s music. The live line-up is Moorings on vocals, guitar and melodica, Mojca Zugna on bass, Mario Usai on guitar and bass, and Sean Winzer on keyboards, synth drums and backing vocals. Twenty-five years on, “Notes From The Underground” sits between “Creatures” and “Farewell” in that sequence.

items.body:
A new concert spotlighting trans, non-binary, and gender non-conforming artists is coming to Singapore.

The inaugural T4T4T4T show will take place on 6 October at Room 526, bringing together RENE, Marian Carmel, haldi honey, and Australia's FVNERAL for a night of live music and community.

Announced by Singapore independent artist RENE, the concert is billed as the first of its kind in the country.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by RENE (@reneannwong)

“We're so excited to bring this show to life,” shared RENE. “It's rare to see diverse and queer identities celebrated on stage in Singapore, so we're doing this to bring our community together for a night of great music.”

They added: “We hope this show might also inspire the organisation of more shows that platform trans, non-binary, and gender non-conforming artists, it would be amazing if we can do a T4T4T4T part 2! And so on!”

The lineup spans indie rock, math-pop, indie-pop, and more. Australian indie rock outfit FVNERAL is the brainchild of trans non-binary songwriter and producer Tay Blunt, who is also the founder and director of TRANSGENRE, Australia's first festival with an entirely trans lineup.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by RENE (@reneannwong)

Singapore math-pop band haldi honey, founded by Daxa, will also take the stage, alongside Philippines-born, Singapore-based singer-songwriter and visual artist Marian Carmel. Rounding out the lineup is RENE, whose sound draws from pop, indie, and rock.

Beyond the music, T4T4T4T will also give back to the community. Ten per cent of ticket proceeds will go to TransBefrienders, a local charity providing accessible health and social support to transgender and gender-diverse individuals.

Purchase tickets here.

The title track is not on the level of Four Momentsbut has done nice passages but parts of it bore me. For me "Hello Phimistar" is the best thing onthe album. items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — *Here Comes the Rain* is most likely the final album by Magnum, a British hard rock band formed in 1972, with 25 studio albums to its credit if you count the two albums released in 1997 and 1999 under the name Hard Rain. With about ten tracks per album, that brings the total to around 250 songs, almost all of which were composed by guitarist Tony Clarkin (he only let Russ Ballard help him with a few minor tracks on the 1990 album *Goodnight L.A.*). This simple calculation highlights just how prolific a songwriter Clarkin was?a rarity in this field. I wrote "was" because Tony suddenly passed away in early January 2024, four days before the release of this quasi-posthumous album.Beyond the context of this tragic event, dedicating a few lines to Magnum in a French magazine devoted to progressive music?even in the broadest sense?is debatable. It's true that aside from the first two albums, *Kingdom of Madness* (1978) and *Magnum II* (1979)?to which one might possibly add the less simplistic half of *The Eleventh Hour* (1983) and *On a Storyteller's Night* (1985)? four highly recommended albums in which the British band seemed to put their own spin on the American formula for full-bodied pop-prog that Styx and Boston had devised with the success we all know, the rest of Magnum's discography offered nothing more than yet another high-energy AOR album.Carefully crafted melodies, a rigid structure that very often followed the verse/chorus/verse/bridge/chorus pattern, and tight, driving rhythms?all of this was far from enough for an audience seeking progressive musical brilliance, despite the regular inclusion on each album of one or two more adventurous tracks with slightly more complex structures.Since the arrival of keyboardist Rick Benton in 2018 (replacing Mark Stanway), Magnum had infused its epic stadium rock with more and more symphonic elements, leaning more often toward the sound of an energized Asia, which made each release more interesting. With its rich sound, finely crafted and catchy melodies, and flawless performance, Magnum came closer than ever to a sophisticated and universal form of heavy prog, quite close to the best of Uriah Heep, another intrepid English veteran. The ambitious *The Serpent Rings* (2020) is a good example of this."Here Comes the Rain" is cut from the same cloth. At first glance, the opening track "Run Into the Shadows," with its unstoppable riff and luminous melody, doesn't seem to represent a major musical shift. Yet hidden deep within this binary music lies a sort of irrepressible despair, a discreet melancholy. And these lyrics, chanted in a thunderous voice, describe our violent world with such darkness that it all seeps into the flashy metal on the surface. This feeling is amply confirmed by the next track, the haunting "Here Comes the Rain," with an even more progressive sound. And what can be said about "Some Kind of Treachery," a heart-wrenching waltz blending symphonic strings and romantic piano?Tony Clarkin once again wrote and composed the entire album but allowed Benton to bring more diversity and boldness to the arrangements (a Hammond organ solo on the boogie-prog track "Bleu Tango," a Moog solo on "Borderline," or classical organ arpeggios on "I Wanna Live," harp-synth sound on "Broken City," and a rhythm-and-blues brass section on "The Seventh Darkness"). Keyboards take center stage ("After the Silence," "Broken City"), while the guitars often remain in the background or provide rhythmic accompaniment, sometimes acoustic ("Here Comes the Rain," "Broken City"). This trend, combined with a greater proportion of slow, melancholic tracks with highly evocative titles (the tragic "Broken City," the anxious "Here Comes the Rain"), and more necessarily binary ones ("Some Kind of Treachery"), where singer Bob Catley?a longtime member of the band whose powerful vocals remain undiminished despite his 76 years?also knows how to be more delicate and moving?all of this makes this dark album more endearing than its predecessors.How can one remain unmoved while listening to "I Wanna Live," with its premonitory undertones, sung with rage by Catley and written by the man who would soon leave this life? I wanna live/ I wanna shout (?) / I wanna live my one desire / Come on and take my hand and walk me through the fire. The magnificent "Borderline," which evokes Rainbow, or even Fish, with its electro-tribal intro and its coda featuring delicate classical piano, brings the flawless *Here Comes the Rain* to a regal close?a bitter and pessimistic swan song, yet one devoid of weakness or clumsiness throughout these fifty memorable minutes.Magnum enjoyed little success in France but great success among our German neighbors, where the majority of their releases reached the top 5 on the sales charts. *Here Comes the Rain* even peaked at No. 2 there upon its release. It is well deserved. After a prolific career, spent largely in the service of a band he could be proud of, Tony Clarkin thus bowed out with what will certainly remain one of Magnum's best albums?an important band worth discovering if you haven't already.
items._cn_summary: 本文乐评讨论了英国硬摇滚乐队Magnum 2024年专辑《Here Comes the Rain》，因吉他手兼词曲核心Tony Clarkin于专辑发布前四天去世，这张作品带有准遗作性质。乐评人梳理了Magnum五十余年的创作轨迹，指出Clarkin是罕见的极高产词曲创作者，总计留下约250首作品。乐评对Magnum在Progressive Rock范围内的定位持审慎态度，认为除早期几张作品外，大部分专辑更接近高能量的AOR路线，采用标准的verse/chorus结构。自2018年键盘手Rick Benton加入后，乐队开始在体育场摇滚中融入更多交响化元素，向Asia和Uriah Heep靠拢。专辑开场曲以强劲riff与明亮旋律包裹着深层忧郁与绝望情绪，后续曲目延续类似手法，将沉重主题与华丽金属声响结合。整体属于带有前progressive意味的交响化硬摇滚/AOR。

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 这并非传统意义上的专辑乐评，而是一档名为《Racing into the Big Muddy》的广播节目曲目列表，内容涵盖从河流到沼泽的音乐主题。节目汇集了Dr John、Jake Blount、Johnny Cash、Paul Simon、Steve Earle等美国根源音乐与民谣艺人，同时纳入巴西、希腊、法国、西非曼丁等地区的世界音乐作品，包括Luiza & Edgar Valente、Martha Mavroidi、Compagnie Chez Bousca、Salim Kouyaté等。来自芬兰的Maria Kalaniemi与Pekko Käppi带来北欧民间元素。整体编排呈现地域多元的拼贴式电台节目形态，以人文地理线索串联不同传统的录音，但缺乏深度评论或艺术分析，信息密度较低，仅为节目单性质的简介。
